summary: The repaired Phase 1 artifact now has a strong measured chassis and keybed silhouette: the 3.0951 aspect ratio, 94% desktop width, 54/46 deck-to-keybed allocation, continuous red rails, six ordered sections, exactly 43 white plus 30 black keys, and only Program/Synth OLEDs are all visible in the refreshed evidence. The data model and interaction pass are materially better, with section-specific drawbars, faders, knobs, toggles, keyboard focus/press states, OLED coupling, and explicit focus outlines. It remains a stylized product-study rather than a close recreation of the reference: most photographed micro-hardware and printed legends are absent or clipped by panel overflow, performance controls are generic sliders rather than a pitch stick/mod wheel, and the narrow capture is a horizontally scrolling 820px canvas. Independent test, typecheck, lint, and build checks all pass.

criteria.label: Silhouette and proportions
evidence: evidence/stage1-desktop.png shows a continuous red chassis, end cheeks, top rail, bottom rail, and complete keybed fully inside the 1440x900 viewport at approximately 94% width.
IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md and styles.css encode the measured 3.0951 aspect ratio and 54/46 control-deck/keybed allocation; the 43-white/30-black E-to-E keyboard is visibly complete.
Compared with the reference crop, the control deck is still more vertically open and the rails/cheeks are simplified, so this is strong but not exceptional fidelity.

criteria.label: Panel layout and density
evidence: The desktop render has the correct six-section order and 13/21/15/9/21/21 grid, with clear Performance, Organ, Piano, Program/Morph, Synth, and Layer Effects boundaries.
sectionDefs contains section-specific drawbars, piano selectors, program navigation/live controls, synth oscillator/filter/envelope/LFO/arp controls, and effect controls.

Most of those controls are hidden by .panel-content overflow in the short deck (for example Organ/Piano/Program), and the visible density remains far below the reference photograph's tightly packed hardware.

criteria.label: Control materials and color
evidence: styles.css provides red chassis, slate inset panels, metallic gradients for knobs/faders/drawbars, key shading, and teal OLED treatment close to the reference palette.

The render lacks the reference's many discrete LED ladders, silver toggle hardware, varied drawbar caps, real pitch stick/mod wheel geometry, and dense material micro-detail; performance pitch/mod are vertical range sliders.

criteria.label: Typography and displays
evidence: Only Program and Synth render OLED elements, and the Synth display changes from SYNTH / WAVE to SYNTH / ARP when Arpeggiator is toggled; no forbidden Organ/Piano/Effects OLED is present.

Section headings use a condensed display face and the required Nord Stage 4 caption/branding is present, but the photograph's tiny legends, display framing, program metadata, and typography hierarchy are largely omitted.

criteria.label: Visible hardware inventory
evidence: The model declares exactly 43 white keys and 30 black offsets, nine Organ drawbars, two OLEDs, and named controls for Piano, Program, Synth, and Effects groups.

In evidence/stage1-desktop.png the 73-key inventory and drawbar bank are visible, but most required section-specific hardware is either represented by small generic switches or clipped below the panel viewport; the performance stick/wheel are not true Nord hardware.

criteria.label: Visual state coverage
evidence: White and black keys depress on pointer and keyboard events; buttons expose aria-pressed and illuminated LED classes; knobs respond to arrow keys/clicks; range controls provide drawbar/fader/wheel movement.
Program and Synth OLED copy is coupled to canonical button state, and explicit button/input/[role=button] focus-visible outlines are implemented in styles.css.
Coverage is still shallow for hover, contextual displays, and section-specific LED/state coupling beyond the representative toggles.

criteria.label: Control interaction
evidence: main.tsx routes pointer press/release, keyboard press/release, range input changes, knob keyboard/click adjustment, and aria-pressed button toggles through one state record.
The eight passing Vitest cases exercise white and black key transitions, button LED state, OLED coupling, named controls, and keyboard focus paths.
Many controls only alter their own local value and do not drive broader hardware feedback; knobs are tested for visibility rather than asserting a changed value.

criteria.label: Responsive accessibility
evidence: Desktop evidence is fully visible without vertical clipping, controls have aria-labels, black keys are focusable role=button elements, and explicit focus-visible styling is present.

The 390x844 evidence intentionally presents an 820px instrument canvas with a horizontal scrollbar, so most of the instrument is off-screen until scrolled and narrow operation is not a compact responsive layout.

criteria.label: Component and data structure
evidence: main.tsx uses stable section.control IDs, a data-driven sectionDefs model, reusable Panel/Knob/SmallButton primitives, and one normalized state map.

The implementation is understandable and avoids invented OLED locations, but almost all rendering remains concentrated in one file and the data model does not encode measured per-control placement or visibility constraints.

criteria.label: Runtime quality
evidence: Independent pnpm run test (8 tests), pnpm run typecheck, pnpm run lint, and pnpm run build all pass; dist/index.html is generated.

The audit reports a browser smoke capture with no app console errors and the desktop render has no clipping; runtime risk remains because the narrow canvas relies on overflow and there is no automated browser console/layout assertion.

issues.title: Expose the full section-specific hardware inventory
issues.detail: Remove panel overflow clipping and fit the required Organ LED/model/percussion, Piano detail, Program live/morph, Synth filter/envelope, and two grouped Effects controls into the visible deck with photo-matched placement and density.

issues.title: Replace generic performance sliders with Nord landmarks
issues.detail: Model a true pitch stick and modulation wheel on exposed red metal, plus the reference branding and nearby master controls.

issues.title: Add reference micro-detail and typography
issues.detail: Add LED ladders, silver switches, varied drawbar caps, printed legends, display framing, and the reference's compact label hierarchy/materials.

issues.title: Improve narrow viewport behavior
issues.detail: Provide a practical 390px presentation or clearly managed section navigation instead of requiring an 820px horizontally scrolling canvas.

issues.title: Deepen behavioral assertions
issues.detail: Assert actual knob/range value changes, state/display coupling across representative controls, and browser-level console/no-clipping behavior in addition to the current unit checks.
